source.title: Multiplier Sequences, Classes of Generalized Bessel Functions and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let {gamma_k}_{k>=0} be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that f(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k / k! is entire. For a real parameter p with -p not a nonnegative integer, define the generalized Bessel-type function F_p(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k / (k! Gamma(k+p+1)). Characterize exactly which nonnegative sequences {gamma_k} have the property that F_p belongs to the Laguerre-Pólya class, that is, has only real zeros in the sense relevant to real-rootedness-preserving entire functions.

accepted.question_text: A sequence {gamma_k}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence if the diagonal operator sending x^k to gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness of every real-rooted polynomial. Determine whether the specific sequence {ln(k+2)/k!}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence, equivalently whether the entire function sum_{k>=0} (ln(k+2)/k!) x^k / k! lies in the appropriate Laguerre-Pólya class.

accepted.question_text: Let {alpha_k}_{k>=0} and {beta_k}_{k>=0} be multiplier sequences of nonnegative real numbers, meaning that each corresponding diagonal operator preserves real-rootedness of real-rooted polynomials. Characterize all functions Psi: R x R -> R such that the termwise transformed sequence {Psi(alpha_k, beta_k)}_{k>=0} is again a multiplier sequence.

Let p(x)=sum_{j=0}^n a_j x^j be a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. Find conditions on p that guarantee the sequence {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence, and find conditions on p that guarantee the same sequence is a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS), meaning that the diagonal operator x^k -> (p(k)/k!) x^k never increases the number of nonreal zeros of a real polynomial.

evidence.quote: Part (b) of Problem 36 appears to be particularly challenging.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_{k>=0} is a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that its associated diagonal operator cannot increase the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial.

Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence and whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence. Equivalently for the multiplier-sequence part, determine whether the entire function phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} sqrt(k) x^k / (k!)^2 belongs to the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients.

accepted.question_text: A multiplier sequence {gamma_k}_{k>=0} is said to have a C_k-representation if there exist functions phi and Phi in the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s), where C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s) is the coefficient sequence defined earlier in the paper from the generating relation e^(((1-t)+(1-s))x) phi(tx) Phi(sx). Characterize exactly which multiplier sequences admit such a C_k-representation.
